Old
OHLD
adj.
Webster 1828 treats OLD as adjective: advanced far in years; long made or used / decayed by time; of long continuance; not new or fresh; of a former year’s growth; ancient; of any duration (how old art thou?); subsisting before something else (the old law repealed by the new); long practiced; long cultivated; and, of old, long ago. His biblical illustration is Genesis 12:4, Abraham seventy-five years old. This page fills the KJV-gap adjective of age and the old man. Companion pages already treat age, child, and man.

Biblical Definition

Old in Scripture is not a brand and not a slur. It names the years the Lord carries, the child who will not depart, and the man in Adam who must be put off. The psalmist will not let gray hair write abandonment: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken (Psa 37:25). The proverb will not let training be a mood: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it (Pro 22:6). The apostle will not let the former conversation keep the pulpit: put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts (Eph 4:22). Colossians will not let the deeds stay: ye have put off the old man with his deeds (Col 3:9). Isaiah will not let hoar hairs be a threat: even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you (Isa 46:4). The dictionary therefore keeps old from becoming either a youth-cult insult or a costume for the Adamic self. It is the Bible’s way of saying: years under God — and a man who must die.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines OLD as advanced in years; long used or decayed by time; of long continuance; not new; ancient; of any duration; prior to something else; long practiced; and of old, from ancient times. He illustrates from Genesis 12:4.

expand to see more

OLD, adjective

1. Advanced far in years or life; having lived beyond the middle period, or rather towards the end of life, or towards the end of the ordinary term of living; applied to animals or plants; as an old man; an old age; an old camel or horse; an old tree.

Abraham was seventy five years old when he departed from Haran. Genesis 12:4.

2. Having been long made or used; decayed by time; as an old garment; an old house.

3. Being of long continuance; begun long ago; as an old acquaintance.

4. Having been long made; not new or fresh; as old wine.

6. Ancient; that existed in former ages; as the old inhabitants of Britain; the old Romans.

7. Of any duration whatever; as a year old; seven years old. How old art thou?

8. Subsisting before something else. He built a new house on the site of the old one. The old law is repealed by the new.

Of old, long ago; from ancient times; as in days of old.

Key Scripture

Psalm 37:25 — "I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread."

Proverbs 22:6 — "Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it."

Ephesians 4:22 — "That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;"

Colossians 3:9 — "Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds;"

Isaiah 46:4 — "And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you."

Modern Corruption

Old is corrupted when years are treated as disposable, when the old man is recast as a personality type, and when hoar hairs are emptied of the God who carries.

expand to see more

The first corruption is the youth-cult. Psalm 37:25 is a man now old who has not seen the righteous forsaken. The age discards gray hair and calls it progress. Isaiah 46:4 remains: even to your old age I am he. Years are not a defect in the people God carries.

The second corruption is Ephesians 4:22 as branding. The old man is corrupt according to deceitful lusts, put off with his deeds (Col 3:9). Therapeutic talk keeps old as a vibe — old-fashioned, old energy — and drops Adam. The dictionary will not. The old man is a nature, not a playlist.

The third corruption is Proverbs 22:6 as a slogan without a way. When he is old, he will not depart from it assumes a child trained in the way he should go. Sentiment keeps the proverb and loses the catechism. Age without the way is just more time in the old man.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: advanced in years / long used / ancient. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew zaqen (H2204) at Psalm 37:25 and Proverbs 22:6; Hebrew ziqnah (H2209) at Isaiah 46:4; Greek palaios (G3820) at Ephesians 4:22 and Colossians 3:9. Genesis 12:4 is Webster’s illustration; this page does not mint a number for that line beyond what the cache tags on the quotations used.

expand to see more

Hebrew zaqen (H2204) — to be old (Psa 37:25; Pro 22:6, when he is old).

Hebrew ziqnah (H2209) — old age (Isa 46:4, old age).

Greek palaios (G3820) — old, worn, former (Eph 4:22; Col 3:9, the old man).

No extra lemma is invented for English old where the cache does not tag it.

Usage

"The psalmist has been young and is now old, and the righteous are not forsaken (Psa 37:25)."

"A child trained in the way will not depart when he is old (Pro 22:6)."

"Put off the old man with his deeds (Eph 4:22; Col 3:9); to old age the LORD carries His people (Isa 46:4)."
